idiom_name: thin wrapper class with explicit target methods (typing.Protocol target)
implementation_notes: Python's duck typing means the target is simply the protocol the caller uses, so the adapter is a thin wrapper: implement the member names the client expects and delegate to the adaptee, using typing.Protocol (or an ABC) to document and statically check that target. The standard library itself adapts binary streams to text through io.TextIOWrapper. When most calls pass through unchanged, __getattr__ forwarding keeps the adapter tiny, but special methods are looked up on the type and bypass __getattr__, so anything used through syntax - len(), indexing, iteration - must be defined explicitly. A wrapper class is still justified whenever one translation point should be documented and tested; a plain function is enough when only a single operation differs.
pitfalls: __getattr__ is not consulted for special methods looked up on the type: len(adapter), adapter[i] and iteration need their own dunder implementations.
A __getattr__ that touches self._adaptee before __init__ ran recurses; copy.copy() and pickle construct instances without __init__, so guard the lookup or define __reduce__.
Forwarded attributes are shared, not encapsulated: adapter.items.append(...) mutates the adaptee's object.
Wrapping breaks identity checks: code doing isinstance(obj, ConcreteType) still fails on the adapter, so adapt at boundaries that were designed for abstraction.

variants.name: Automatic delegation via __getattr__
variants.implementation_notes: For adapters that must forward most of the protocol unchanged, implement only the translated members and let __getattr__ delegate the rest to the wrapped object - the documented 'forward the rest' idiom, and the smallest adapter Python can write. The boundary is implicit: dunders are not forwarded, attribute writes need __setattr__, and the class must survive copying and pickling. Choose it when the target protocol is large and mostly pass-through; write the explicit class when the translation itself is the point.
pitfalls: Dunder lookups bypass __getattr__: implement __len__/__getitem__/__iter__ explicitly when clients use syntax.
Unpickling and copy.copy build instances without __init__, so a naive lookup recurses to RecursionError.
__setattr__ is not mirrored, so writes land on the adapter unless you delegate them too - decide which side owns the state.
